anomalies.observed: In the netlist, J8 (channel 2) connects through R6 to /NET0007, which is tied to bus pins 19 (via R15) and 21 (via R9). J1 (channel 1) connects through R23 to /NET0032, which is tied to bus pins 20 (via R7) and 22 (via R8). Thus channel 1 uses pins 20/22 and channel 2 uses pins 19/21.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that channel 1 should use M5Stack bus pins 19/21 and channel 2 should use pins 20/22.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: If the jumpers are populated as intended for a given M5Stack core, PWM1 and PWM2 will be swapped: PWM1 will drive the channel-2 servo header (J8) and PWM2 will drive channel-1 (J1). This reverses pan and tilt unless the servo cables or firmware are adjusted.

parsed.summary: The design files contain a functional anomaly: the PWM channel-to-M5Stack-bus-pin mapping is swapped relative to the specification, so channel 1 uses pins 20/22 and channel 2 uses pins 19/21 instead of the specified 19/21 for channel 1 and 20/22 for channel 2. This would swap pan and tilt when the jumpers are populated as intended.

response.reasoning:
We need review design files vs spec. Need identify anomalies. Let's parse carefully.

We have netlist with refs different from spec? Spec references J1/J2 M-BUS connectors, J3/J8 servo, J5 BAT, J6 PortB, J7 5V_POWER, D1 SS54, D2 PMEG3030EP, etc. But netlist refs:
- J4 and J6 are 2x15 M-BUS connectors? Spec said J1/J2 for M-BUS. Netlist has J4 and J6 as Conn_02x15. J1/J8 are Conn_01x03 servo headers? Wait J1 value Conn_01x03 footprint JST EH 3-pin. J8 Conn_01x03. J3 value BAT, Conn_01x02 PH. J2 value 5V_POWER, Conn_01x02 XH. J11 Conn_01x04 PH horizontal (PortB). So reference designators shifted/inconsistent with spec. But spec says source design maybe different refs? Need not report style/ref mismatch unless actual connectivity wrong. We need decide anomaly: deviation from intended design that makes board behave differently. Could be wrong component values/connections.

Let's understand actual netlist.

Components:
C2 100u
C3 100u
C5 100u? Wait spec says C5 0.1u decoupling MAX3485. Netlist C5 value "100u" footprint 1206 same as bulk caps. C8 value "0.1u" footprint 0603. So C5 changed from 0.1u to 100u. Also C5 is on net GND and Net-(D1-K) i.e. servo power rail? Let's inspect: net code 32 Net-(D1-K): nodes C2.1, C3.2, C5.2, C7.2, D1-K, J1.2, J8.2. Wait D1 in netlist is PMEG3030EP (value PMEG3030EP) not SS54. D3 is SS54. C5 pin2 on Net-(D1-K) (servo rail). C5 pin1 on GND. So C5 is 100u bulk on servo rail, not 0.1u decoupling on +3V3. C8 0.1u is on +3V3 to GND. Spec says C5 0.1u decoupling on +3V3 (MAX3485 supply). Netlist C8 is that. So C5 value changed? Maybe reference designators differ; the 0.1u decoupling exists as C8, so not necessarily missing; but spec table says C1–C4 100u bulk, C5 0.1u decoupling. Netlist has C2,C3,C5,C7 100u bulk (four 100u) and C8 0.1u. So there are four 100u caps, one 0.1u. Spec says C1–C4 four 100u and C5 0.1u. Netlist has C2,C3,C5,C7 100u plus C8 0.1u. So the 0.1u decoupling is C8 not C5. Reference designator mismatch but functionally has four 100u bulk and one 0.1u decoupling. Not anomaly unless C5 should be 0.1u but C8 covers. Need check if extra 100u? Count four 100u yes. C5 is one of bulk. So okay? Spec says C1-C4 but netlist C2,C3,C5,C7. Ref designators differ, but no functional difference (same number). However spec table specifically says C5 0.1u decoupling on +3V3 (MAX3485 supply). In netlist, C8 0.1u on +3V3. So maybe C5 wrong value but C8 extra? Actually C8 is in netlist as 0.1u; spec didn't mention C8. Could be reference designator shift: original C5 might correspond to C8. We shouldn't report ref mismatch if function correct. But maybe an anomaly: C5 (100u) is a large cap on servo rail, but spec didn't list extra 100u? Wait spec says C1–C4 100 µF × 4; netlist has four 100u caps. It's just refs C2,C3,C5,C7 instead of C1-C4. So no electrical anomaly.

Now inspect larger.

Power:
+3V3 net: C8.1, J4.11, J6.11, Q3.2 (E of PNP BC857), R11.1, R16.1, R17.1, U2.8 (VCC). +3V3 is M5Stack bus 3.3V. Q3 emitter to +3V3, PNP for direction control. R16 pull-up from +3V3 to U2-B. R17 from +3V3 to /NET0001 (A line). R11 from +3V3 to /NET0009 (U2 DI/TXD2). This is odd: MAX3485 DI input tied to +3V3 via R11 10k and to /NET0009? Wait /NET0009 nodes: J4.15, J6.15, R11.2, R22.1, U2.4 DI. J4 pin15/TXD2. R11 10k pull-up on TXD2 line to 3.3V, okay. R22 5.1k from TXD2 to Q3.B (base). Q3 emitter to +3V3, collector to DE/RE pins. This matches spec: Q2 BC857 PNP, driven from /TXD2 via R1 10k, R2 5.1k toggles DE/RE. Here Q3 with R11 10k and R22 5.1k. Fine.

+5V net: D1? Wait D1 value PMEG3030EP, pin2 A on +5V, pin1 K on servo rail Net(D1-K). So D1 is the servo rail diode, spec D2 (PMEG3030EP) from +5V into servo rail. D3 value SS54, pin1 K on +5V, pin2 A on Net-(D3-A) -> J2.1. So D3 is external 5V input diode, spec D1. Again refs swapped. Functionally: external 5V J2 -> D3 SS54 -> +5V. +5V to servo rail via D1 PMEG3030EP -> Net(D1-K) -> J1.2/J8.2 and caps. That matches spec (D1 external SS54, D2 PMEG3030EP servo) except refs swapped. So okay.

Servo signal path:
- J1 (Conn_01x03) is channel? J1 pin3? Net code 34 Net-(J1-Pin_3): J1.3, R23.1, R24.2, R3.1. R23 value 1k? Wait R23 is 1k, R24 0, R3 0. Spec says PWM path: R3/R4 1k series from PWM GPIO to J3/J8 pin3. Netlist: J1 pin3 connects to R23 (1k) and R24 (0) and R3(0)? Need map.

- Net code 35 Net-(J3-Pin_1): J3.1, Q2.S, R19.2. This is battery input to Q2 source? But J3 is BAT connector, Q2 is P-FET battery disconnect. Spec says J5 battery through Q1 to /BAT bus. Signal path for servo: The two servo headers are J1 and J8? J1 is 3-pin (value Conn_01x03) footprint EH. J8 is 3-pin EH. J1.2 on servo rail Net(D1-K), J8.2 on servo rail. J1.1 and J8.1 on GND. So J1/J8 are servo headers, not M-BUS. Spec says J3/J8 servo headers; netlist J1/J8. Ref mismatch.

Standard RS-485 fail-safe biasing uses pull-up on one line and pull-down on the other. So R16 to +3V3 on B and R1 to GND? Wait standard: A pulled high, B pulled low (or vice versa) to define idle. Here A has pull-up 2k to 3.3V, B has divider 2.2k to 3.3V and 2.2k to GND. That makes B at 1.65V, A at 3.3V, differential ~1.65V. Could be okay? If only A is used as single-wire TTL, why B biased?
